flow_summary: The interviewer was patient and persistent in guiding a difficult, disorganized patient, but the interview suffered from significant mechanical issues during the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 sections. The system repeatedly failed to present the questionnaire items clearly, leading to excessive, redundant questioning and confusion that could have been avoided with better framing.

issues.evidence: In the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 sections, the interviewer frequently had to re-ask the same question multiple times because the initial presentation was confusing or the patient struggled with the format. For example, PHQ-9 Question 3 was asked three times (turns 6, 7, and 8).

The interviewer often presented the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 items in a way that caused the patient to repeatedly ask for clarification on the timeframe or the scale, indicating the initial prompts were not sufficiently clear for this persona.

The transition into the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 sections felt mechanical and repetitive, with the interviewer struggling to maintain a natural conversational rhythm while trying to force the patient into the required response format.
